children: Chinese electric vehicle maker Li Auto
is set to report its third-quarter results on Wednesday before the market opens.

calls for a loss of $0.13 per share, while revenue is expected to increase 8.7% Y/Y to $4.13B. Over the last two years, Li Auto has beaten EPS estimates 63% of the time and revenue estimates 50% of the time.
During the quarter, Li Auto continued to expand its

lineup with the launch of the Li i6 and refreshed models. The company also introduced its proprietary Lianshan Battery and Lianshan Motor technologies, while advancing its smart-driving capabilities. In November, it plans to roll out an OTA update featuring the upgraded MACH VLA 2.5 and enhanced cockpit Agent features.
Despite the innovations, Chinese EV makers continue to face intense competition in the domestic market. Moreover, a
in car sales in China is also taking a toll on the companies.
Beijing-based Li Auto delivered 29,025 vehicles in October 2026, representing an 8.6% Y/Y decline from 31,767 units in October 2025 and an 8.8% M/M drop from 31,817 units in September 2026.
Seeking Alpha analysts and Seeking Alpha's Quant ratings are cautious and rated the stock a Hold. In contrast, Wall Street analysts consider it a Buy.

"With a refreshed product lineup and solid growth in deliveries in Q3, I believe Li Auto could be set for a revaluation to the upside, on the condition that the EV maker generates a turnaround in its margin profile," said Seeking Alpha analyst The Asian Investor.

Meanwhile, another Seeking Alpha analyst Ricardo Fernandez argued that consensus growth expectations for 2027 are overly optimistic. He cites intense competition, stagnant domestic demand, and limited overseas traction as key challenges, with a $6 year-end 2027 price target.
Over the last three months, EPS estimates recorded one upward and two downward revisions, while revenue estimates saw one upward and six downward revisions.
Li Auto shares have declined 37.42% YTD, underperforming the S&P 500's 5.73% gain over the same period.

title: Li Auto Q3 earnings on deck: What to expect
